passages.text: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather, has discovered?
passages.sermon:
Abraham is our forefather.
He lived as a man on earth.
What did Abraham discover?
What can we say about what Abraham found?
passages.original: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν εὑρηκέναι Ἀβραὰμ τὸν προπάτορα ἡμῶν κατὰ σάρκα

passages.text: If Abraham was indeed justified by works, he had something to boast about, but not before God.
passages.sermon: Abraham is our forefather.\r\nIf God justified Abraham by his works, Abraham could boast.\r\nAbraham could not boast before God.
passages.original: εἰ γὰρ Ἀβραὰμ ἐξ ἔργων ἐδικαιώθη ἔχει καύχημα ἀλλ’ οὐ πρὸς Θεόν

passages.text: For what does the Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.”
passages.sermon: The Scripture speaks about Abraham.\r\nAbraham believed God.\r\nGod counted Abraham’s faith as righteousness.
passages.original: τί γὰρ ἡ γραφὴ λέγει Ἐπίστευσεν δὲ Ἀβραὰμ τῷ Θεῷ καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην

passages.text: Now the wages of the worker are not credited as a gift, but as an obligation.
passages.sermon:
A worker receives wages.
The employer does not give wages as a gift.
The employer gives wages because he owes them.
Wages are an obligation, not a favor.
passages.original: Τῷ δὲ ἐργαζομένῳ ὁ μισθὸς οὐ λογίζεται κατὰ χάριν ἀλλὰ κατὰ ὀφείλημα

passages.text: However, to the one who does not work, but believes in Him who justifies the wicked, his faith is credited as righteousness.
passages.sermon:
God justifies wicked people.
A person may not work for righteousness.
This person believes in God.
God credits this person's faith as righteousness.
passages.original: τῷ δὲ μὴ ἐργαζομένῳ πιστεύοντι δὲ ἐπὶ τὸν δικαιοῦντα τὸν ἀσεβῆ λογίζεται ἡ πίστις αὐτοῦ εἰς δικαιοσύνην

passages.text: And David speaks likewise of the blessedness of the man to whom God credits righteousness apart from works: “Blessed are they whose lawless acts are forgiven, whose sins are covered.
passages.sermon:
David was a king and a prophet in Israel.
David spoke about a certain kind of happiness.
This happiness belongs to a person.
God gives this person righteousness.
God does not require works from this person.
David said, “Blessed are those whose lawless acts God has forgiven.
Blessed are those whose sins God has covered.”
passages.original: καθάπερ καὶ Δαυὶδ λέγει τὸν μακαρισμὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ᾧ ὁ Θεὸς λογίζεται δικαιοσύνην χωρὶς ἔργων Μακάριοι ὧν ἀφέθησαν αἱ ἀνομίαι καὶ ὧν ἐπεκαλύφθησαν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι

passages.text: Blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will never count against him.”
passages.sermon:
God is the Lord.
God judges people.
A man can have sin.
The Lord will not count this man's sin against him.
This man is blessed.
passages.original: μακάριος ἀνὴρ οὗ οὐ μὴ λογίσηται Κύριος ἁμαρτίαν

passages.text: Is this blessing only on the circumcised, or also on the uncircumcised? We have been saying that Abraham’s faith was credited to him as righteousness.
passages.sermon:
Paul asks a question about blessing.
He asks if this blessing is only for the circumcised.
He also asks if it is for the uncircumcised.
Paul reminds us about Abraham.
Abraham believed God.
God counted Abraham’s faith as righteousness.
passages.original: Ὁ μακαρισμὸς οὖν οὗτος ἐπὶ τὴν περιτομὴν ἢ καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν ἀκροβυστίαν λέγομεν γάρ Ἐλογίσθη τῷ Ἀβραὰμ ἡ πίστις εἰς δικαιοσύνην

passages.text: In what context was it credited? Was it after his circumcision, or before? It was not after, but before.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was a man of faith.
God credited righteousness to Abraham.
God did this before Abraham was circumcised.
God did not credit righteousness after Abraham was circumcised.
God credited righteousness while Abraham was still uncircumcised.
passages.original: πῶς οὖν ἐλογίσθη ἐν περιτομῇ ὄντι ἢ ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ οὐκ ἐν περιτομῇ ἀλλ’ ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ

passages.text: And he received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness that he had by faith while he was still uncircumcised. So then, he is the father of all who believe but are not circumcised, in order that righteousness might be credited to them.
passages.sermon:
Abraham received circumcision as a sign.
Circumcision was a seal.
This seal showed the righteousness Abraham had by faith.
Abraham had this faith when he was still uncircumcised.
Abraham became the father of all who believe without being circumcised.
God credits righteousness to these believers also.
passages.original: Καὶ σημεῖον ἔλαβεν περιτομῆς σφραγῖδα τῆς δικαιοσύνης τῆς πίστεως τῆς ἐν τῇ ἀκροβυστίᾳ εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν πατέρα πάντων τῶν πιστευόντων δι’ ἀκροβυστίας εἰς τὸ λογισθῆναι καὶ αὐτοῖς τὴν δικαιοσύνην

passages.text: And he is also the father of the circumcised who not only are circumcised, but who also walk in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had before he was circumcised.
passages.sermon:
Abraham is our father.
He is the father of those who are circumcised.
He is not only the father of those who are circumcised.
He is also the father of those who follow his faith.
These people walk in the footsteps of Abraham’s faith.
Abraham had this faith before he was circumcised.
passages.original: καὶ πατέρα περιτομῆς τοῖς οὐκ ἐκ περιτομῆς μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς στοιχοῦσιν τοῖς ἴχνεσιν τῆς ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ πίστεως τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἀβραάμ

passages.text: For the promise to Abraham and his offspring that he would be heir of the world was not given through the law, but through the righteousness that comes by faith.
passages.sermon:
God gave Abraham a promise.
God also gave this promise to Abraham’s descendants.
God said Abraham would inherit the world.
God did not give this promise through the law.
God gave this promise through righteousness.
This righteousness comes by faith.
passages.original: Οὐ γὰρ διὰ νόμου ἡ ἐπαγγελία τῷ Ἀβραὰμ ἢ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ τὸ κληρονόμον αὐτὸν εἶναι κόσμου ἀλλὰ διὰ δικαιοσύνης πίστεως

passages.text: For if those who live by the law are heirs, faith is useless and the promise is worthless, because the law brings wrath. And where there is no law, there is no transgression.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing about Abraham and the promise God gave him.
Paul says some people try to become heirs by following the law.
If people become heirs by the law, then faith has no value.
If people become heirs by the law, then God’s promise means nothing.
The law brings God’s wrath.
Where there is no law, there is no breaking of the law.
passages.original: εἰ γὰρ οἱ ἐκ νόμου κληρονόμοι κεκένωται ἡ πίστις καὶ κατήργηται ἡ ἐπαγγελία ὁ γὰρ νόμος ὀργὴν κατεργάζεται οὗ δὲ οὐκ ἔστιν νόμος οὐδὲ παράβασις

passages.text: Therefore, the promise comes by faith, so that it may rest on grace and may be guaranteed to all Abraham’s offspring—not only to those who are of the law, but also to those who are of the faith of Abraham. He is the father of us all.
passages.sermon:
God gave Abraham a promise.
This promise comes by faith.
God gives this promise by grace.
God wants the promise to be certain for all Abraham’s offspring.
The promise is not only for those who follow the law.
The promise is also for those who have faith like Abraham.
Abraham is the father of us all.
passages.original: Διὰ τοῦτο ἐκ πίστεως ἵνα κατὰ χάριν εἰς τὸ εἶναι βεβαίαν τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν παντὶ τῷ σπέρματι οὐ τῷ ἐκ τοῦ νόμου μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ τῷ ἐκ πίστεως Ἀβραάμ ὅς ἐστιν πατὴρ πάντων ἡμῶν

passages.text: As it is written: “I have made you a father of many nations.” He is our father in the presence of God, in whom he believed, the God who gives life to the dead and calls into being what does not yet exist.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Abraham.
God said, “I have made you a father of many nations.”
Abraham is our father.
He stands before God.
Abraham believed in God.
God gives life to the dead.
God calls things that do not exist as if they exist.
passages.original: καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι Πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν τέθεικά σε κατέναντι οὗ ἐπίστευσεν Θεοῦ τοῦ ζωοποιοῦντος τοὺς νεκροὺς καὶ καλοῦντος τὰ μὴ ὄντα ὡς ὄντα

passages.text: Against all hope, Abraham in hope believed and so became the father of many nations, just as he had been told, “So shall your offspring be.”
passages.sermon:
Abraham is the father of all who believe.
Abraham faced a situation with no hope.
Abraham still chose to hope.
Abraham believed God.
God had told Abraham, “So shall your offspring be.”
Abraham believed this promise.
Because Abraham believed, he became the father of many nations.
passages.original: ὃς παρ’ ἐλπίδα ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι ἐπίστευσεν εἰς τὸ γενέσθαι αὐτὸν πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον Οὕτως ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα σου

passages.text: Without weakening in his faith, he acknowledged the decrepitness of his body (since he was about a hundred years old) and the lifelessness of Sarah’s womb.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was about one hundred years old.
Abraham saw that his own body was as good as dead.
Abraham saw that Sarah’s womb was lifeless.
Abraham did not weaken in his faith.
Abraham acknowledged these things.
passages.original: καὶ μὴ ἀσθενήσας τῇ πίστει κατενόησεν τὸ ἑαυτοῦ σῶμα ἤδη νενεκρωμένον ἑκατονταετής που ὑπάρχων καὶ τὴν νέκρωσιν τῆς μήτρας Σάρρας

passages.text: Yet he did not waver through disbelief in the promise of God, but was strengthened in his faith and gave glory to God, being fully persuaded that God was able to do what He had promised.
passages.sermon:
Abraham heard the promise of God.
He did not doubt God’s promise.
He did not let unbelief weaken him.
He became strong in his faith.
He gave glory to God.
He was completely sure.
He knew God could do what He had promised.
passages.original: εἰς δὲ τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ Θεοῦ οὐ διεκρίθη τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ ἀλλὰ ἐνεδυναμώθη τῇ πίστει δοὺς δόξαν τῷ Θεῷ καὶ πληροφορηθεὶς ὅτι ὃ ἐπήγγελται δυνατός ἐστιν καὶ ποιῆσαι

passages.text: This is why “it was credited to him as righteousness.”
passages.sermon: God saw Abraham’s faith.\r\nGod counted Abraham’s faith as righteousness.\r\nGod credited righteousness to Abraham because of his faith.
passages.original: διὸ καὶ Ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην

passages.text: Now the words “it was credited to him” were written not only for Abraham, but also for us, to whom righteousness will be credited—for us who believe in Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.
passages.sermon:
God made a promise to Abraham.
God said, “It was credited to him.”
These words were not written only for Abraham.
God also wrote them for us.
God will credit righteousness to us too.
God will do this for all who believe in Him.
God raised Jesus, our Lord, from the dead.
We believe in this God.
God will count us as righteous because of our faith.
passages.original: Οὐκ ἐγράφη δὲ δι’ αὐτὸν μόνον ὅτι Ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ ἀλλὰ καὶ δι’ ἡμᾶς οἷς μέλλει λογίζεσθαι τοῖς πιστεύουσιν ἐπὶ τὸν ἐγείραντα Ἰησοῦν τὸν Κύριον ἡμῶν ἐκ νεκρῶν

passages.text: He was delivered over to death for our trespasses and was raised to life for our justification.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is our Lord.
God delivered Jesus over to death.
God did this because of our trespasses.
God raised Jesus to life.
God did this so we could be justified.
passages.original: ὃς παρεδόθη διὰ τὰ παραπτώματα ἡμῶν καὶ ἠγέρθη διὰ τὴν δικαίωσιν ἡμῶν
